prompt: Distinguish between a scalar quantity and a vector quantity. Give one kinematic example of each.
hints: Focus on the requirement for direction.
solution: A scalar quantity has magnitude only, whereas a vector quantity has both magnitude and direction [1 mark]. Kinematic example of a scalar: distance (or speed); kinematic example of a vector: displacement (or velocity, or acceleration) [1 mark].
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: State that scalar has magnitude only, vector has magnitude and direction [1 mark].
Step 2: Provide valid kinematic examples: scalar = distance or speed; vector = displacement, velocity, or acceleration [1 mark].

provenance.independence_statement: Authored independently to test fundamental scalar versus vector distinction.
